learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the operating principles, classification, and application areas of lifting and transport equipment;
Understanding of the constructive components and operating schemes for the main types of installations (cranes, conveyors, elevators, etc.);
Acquisition of calculation and sizing methods for mechanical and structural elements specific to these installations;
Knowledge of safety requirements and technical regulations applicable to lifting and handling equipment.
Ability to analyze and select appropriate technical solutions for different lifting and transport applications;
Use of computer-aided design tools and calculation methods for sizing installation components;
Diagnosis and evaluation of the technical condition of lifting and transport equipment;
Application of occupational safety regulations and technical standards in the operation of these systems.
Taking responsibility for technical decisions regarding the design, maintenance, and operation of lifting installations;
Ability to work in a multidisciplinary team for the realization of technical projects specific to the field;
Demonstration of a proactive attitude towards respecting safety, quality, and energy efficiency requirements;
Development of autonomy in technical documentation and updating knowledge regarding modern material handling equipment.

syllabus_topics: Lifting equipment used in mechanical workshops (jacks, hoists, winches)
Lifting equipment used on construction sites, in warehouses, and in ports (lifting devices, elevators, cranes)
Calculation and verification of cables and chains used in lifting equipment
Mechanical assemblies used for suspending loads
Belt conveyor systems, roller conveyor systems and other transport systems
Adoption of the construction scheme for the lifting installation, support, hook load (Derrick); installation sketch.
Calculation of forces in the jib of a Derrick crane; determination of the maximum stress position in two variants: jib longer than the mast (L>H) and jib shorter than the mast (L<H)
Sizing and buckling verification of the Derrick crane jib constructed from a tubular section bar (L<H)
Sizing and verification of the Derrick crane mast (mast longer than the jib) tubular section bar (L<H)
Calculation of the load suspension cable and the sheaves in the block and tackle (selection of an optimal variant) (L<H)
Calculation of the jib anchoring cable and the sheaves in the block and tackle (selection of an optimal variant) (L<H)
teaching_methods: Discussion of technical solutions and causes of failures

assessment_methods.method: Colocviu/Verification (includes systematic observation, individual/team assignments, report, formative tests, final test)
Project (design activity, project finalization, project presentation)

assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Whole grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with grade 5 certifying the acquisition of the minimum learning outcomes for a discipline and the granting of its study credits. A minimum score of 5 is required for both the Colocviu/Verification and the Project components.
